claims.text: The dynamic response of solidified FeNiCrMn is predominantly governed by a transition from dislocation-mediated plasticity to twinning-induced plasticity.
Increasing strain rate promotes a transition toward twinning-induced plasticity in FeNiCrMn.
Decreasing temperature promotes a transition toward twinning-induced plasticity in FeNiCrMn.
FeNiCrMn has low stacking-fault energy.
The low stacking-fault energy of FeNiCrMn favors mechanical-twin activation under high-rate or low-temperature conditions.
Mechanical twinning enhances strain hardening in FeNiCrMn.
Mechanical twinning enhances the dynamic strength of FeNiCrMn.
Deformation twins act as barriers to dislocation motion.
At lower strain rates and/or higher temperatures, deformation in FeNiCrMn is primarily accommodated by dislocation glide.
Dislocation-glide-dominated deformation produces moderate strain hardening in FeNiCrMn.
Twin boundaries strengthen FeNiCrMn under high-rate or low-temperature deformation.
High-strain-rate, low-temperature testing will produce a greater deformation-twin density than dislocation-dominated conditions.
High-strain-rate, low-temperature testing will produce a higher strain-hardening rate than dislocation-dominated conditions.
High-strain-rate, low-temperature testing will produce higher flow stress than dislocation-dominated conditions.
At room temperature and a quasi-static strain rate, FeNiCrMn deformation is expected to be primarily dislocation-mediated and to have lower twin density.
The proposed mechanism is applicable to homogeneous, Co-free, solidified FeNiCrMn specimens.
Prior processing defects, extreme composition variations, or additional phases may alter stacking-fault energy or twin nucleation and cause deviations from the prediction.
Testing at -50°C, 25°C, and 200°C and at strain rates of 10^-3, 10^2, and 10^3 s^-1 can be used to evaluate the proposed temperature–strain-rate mechanism.
EBSD and TEM can be used after deformation to quantify twin density and characterize dislocation structures.

Failure to observe a significant increase in twin density, or failure of twin density to correlate with enhanced strain hardening and flow stress, would falsify the proposed twinning-driven mechanism.

contradictions.description: The specimens are described simultaneously as casting-homogenized and as-solidified. Homogenization is a post-solidification treatment, so a homogenized specimen is not literally in the as-solidified state unless those terms are defined more carefully.
